brief.statement: A launch site for a ride-sharing app,
brief.muted: built to fill the waitlist before the apps ship.

body: Waytu pairs commuters who live near each other and travel the same way, so they can share the car and split the cost.
It was founded in Accra in 2024 and is launching there first, with other cities in Ghana and Nigeria in its plans.
Five pages: home, about, how it works, safety and contact, plus the legal pages.
Every call to action opens the same waitlist form. It asks whether you own a car and whether you would share rides in it, so the team can tell drivers from riders before launch.
A stranger’s car is a hard sell, so a whole page is given to safety.
list: Sign-up with a phone number and a government-issued ID.
Live location shared with trusted contacts during a ride.
Riders and drivers review each other after every trip.
Costs are split on distance and fuel.

notes.title: Built to answer “is this safe?”
items: A single modal form collects contact details and whether the person has a car to share, from any page.
Sign up and verify, find or offer a ride, connect and coordinate, rate and review: the same flow on the homepage and its own page.
Identity checks, live tracking, an emergency button and guidance for before, during and after a ride.
A contact form with subjects from safety concerns to partnerships, and a live-chat widget on every page.
